title: How to Wash Your Hair and Scalp with Braids In
hero_alt: Braids being rinsed at a salon basin
image_plan: pexels: man braids back of head
card_text: Diluted shampoo on the scalp lines, a gentle rinse and a full dry. How to wash braids without roughing up the rows.
lede: To wash braids, dilute a gentle shampoo with water, apply it directly to the scalp along the parts, and massage with your fingertips rather than scrubbing the braids. Rinse thoroughly with the water running down the braids the way they lie, squeeze the water out gently, and let everything dry completely. The scalp gets clean, the braids barely move, and you avoid the frizz that comes from rubbing.
Here's the step-by-step, why drying matters as much as washing, and the habits that make a set look old early.

blocks.heading: Your scalp keeps working.
paragraphs: Under a set of braids, the scalp keeps making oil and shedding skin like it always does. Sweat and dust add to it, and without washing, it all collects along the parts as buildup and itch.
The challenge is cleaning the scalp without disturbing the braids. Washing the usual way, with lots of rubbing, roughs up the rows and loosens the base.
A clean scalp is also simply more comfortable to live with for the weeks a set is in.

subsections.heading: Dilute the shampoo
paragraphs: Mix a gentle shampoo with water in an applicator or spray bottle. Thinned shampoo spreads along the parts easily and rinses out more completely.

subsections.heading: Apply to the parts
paragraphs: Put it straight onto the scalp lines between the braids. Work in sections so none get missed.

subsections.heading: Massage, don't scrub
paragraphs: Use the pads of your fingers to massage the scalp in small circles. Keep your nails off the skin and leave the braids themselves mostly alone.

subsections.heading: Rinse downward
paragraphs: Let the water run from the roots toward the ends, the way the braids lie. Keep rinsing longer than seems necessary. Leftover shampoo causes itch and flakes.
A handheld shower head makes it easier to aim the water at the scalp.

subsections.heading: Condition lightly, if at all
paragraphs: If you use conditioner, keep it light and rinse it out fully. Heavy conditioner can sit inside the braids.

blocks.heading: The step people rush.
paragraphs: Braids hold water inside long after the surface feels dry. Squeeze them gently in a towel, without wringing or rubbing, then let them dry all the way through.
A dryer on a low or cool setting helps reach the scalp. Covering or sleeping on braids that are still wet inside can leave a musty smell and keeps the scalp damp for hours.
In dry weather the outside of a braid dries fast, but the center still takes time. Feel the thickest braids at the roots before you call it done.
Once they're fully dry, cover them at night to keep the rows smooth.

blocks.heading: What ages a set early.
paragraphs: A few things make braids look older than they are:
bullets: Piling the braids on top of your head to wash them, which twists and tangles the rows.
Scrubbing the braids instead of the scalp.
Using full-strength shampoo that's hard to rinse out.
Heavy product right after washing, which traps moisture and builds up.
Washing right before bed with no time left to dry.

blocks.heading: When washing won't fix it.
paragraphs: Washing keeps a set clean, but it can't tighten a loose base or redraw parts that have filled in. When that happens, it's time for a fresh set.

items.q: How do you wash braids without frizz?
items.a: Diluted shampoo on the scalp only, a fingertip massage, a long rinse downward, and a gentle squeeze dry.

items.q: Can I wash braids with regular shampoo?
items.a: Yes, thinned with water so it spreads along the parts and rinses out fully.
Squeeze them in a towel, then let them dry completely, using a dryer on low if you need to.

items.q: Why does my scalp itch with braids in?
items.a: Buildup and leftover shampoo are common causes. If the itch is severe or the scalp is sore, see a doctor.
